lineage agent notes: 1) claims_paid_eur takes stg.claim_payments.amount as-is. Despite the name, nothing converts it to EUR and claim_payments has no currency column. The same unconverted amount feeds paid_to_written and review_flag. 2) The stg.brokers LEFT JOIN doesn't remove rows, but brokers has a _row_seq column, so it may hold several versions per broker_code. If it does, output rows are duplicated. I listed the join as a low-confidence filter. 3) Claims count toward claims_notified, and their payments toward claims_paid_eur, only if reported_date falls in the year. Payments in the year on claims reported earlier are dropped. 4) If no fx rate is found for a non-EUR currency, the product is NULL and SUM skips it, so that premium is lost from gwp_eur without any error. 5) policies_in_force and claims_notified are COUNT(*) values defaulted to 0 by ISNULL, so they have no column that derives them. The in-force and claims date filters still decide which rows are counted. 6) The output's broker_code and lob_code are the union of keys across in-force, premium, notified and paid, so every filter on those sets helps decide which rows appear.

warnings:
lineage agent notes: The ROW_NUMBER at lines 76-77 groups by (period, claim_id) only, not by reserve_type. So each claim keeps just its single latest reserve row, whatever its type. The header says expense reserves count towards incurred (CR-0577), but they are only included when the expense reserve happens to be the latest row. The SUM at lines 85-86 then always adds up exactly one row per period. The PySpark version must copy this exactly, not fix it. Ties on reserve_date are broken by reserve_id DESC.

When computing last_payment_date, payments with a NULL amount are skipped (line 67), but they still count as nil in the sums.

days_since_last_activity is NULL when the claim has no payments and no reserves. The 1900-01-01 sentinel only affects the comparison and never reaches the output.

The filter edges on payment_date, reserve_date and the claim_id joins in the payment and reserve steps decide which payment and reserve rows feed the sums. They change which rows appear only indirectly, through the incurred_amount >= 25000 threshold at line 134.

warnings: translator notes: The status filter compares on upper(rtrim(status)). It deliberately does not use ltrim, so leading spaces count, as they do in SQL Server (X2-D3). If status or closed_date is NULL, three-valued logic handles it the same way in both engines. The NOW/PRIOR CROSS APPLY is a crossJoin with a two-row spark.createDataFrame of (period, as_at). The ROW_NUMBER tiebreak is reserve_date DESC, reserve_id DESC, then _row_seq ASC; _row_seq only matters when two rows share both reserve_date and reserve_id. As in T-SQL, the SUMs and ISNULLs are cast to decimal(38,2). The 1.10 and 0.90 factors are Decimal literals, so the category comparisons stay exact. The 1900-01-01 sentinel is built from the legacy literal '19000101' with to_date. days_since_last_activity is datediff(as_of, last_activity_date), and it is NULL when a claim has no payments and no reserves. Duplicate claim_ids in stg.claims would multiply rows through the joins exactly as the legacy code does. Note for reviewers: SUM(CASE ... reserve_amount ...) can return NULL when the only rn = 1 row has a NULL amount; ISNULL in #inc turns that into 0, and the Spark version does the same.

warnings:
translator notes: 1) #pol: if stg.products has more than one row matching a product_code (case or trailing-space variants, or duplicates), the legacy ROW_NUMBER picks one of them arbitrarily, because the ORDER BY only uses snapshot columns. I added p._row_seq ASC as a final tie-break so the result is deterministic; on such data, check that lob_code matches legacy.
2) paid_to_written: T-SQL divides decimal(38,2) by decimal(38,10), which gives decimal(38,6) truncated toward zero. I reproduce this exactly with an integral division, (num*1000000) div den (this truncates toward zero), then divide by 1000000 and cast to decimal(12,4), which rounds half up. A zero denominator becomes NULL (NULLIF) and the flag is 'N'.
3) gwp is kept in decimal throughout: decimal(31,10) products, summed as decimal(38,10), then cast to decimal(14,2) half up. The fx OUTER APPLY is partitioned by the transaction's _row_seq, which I assume is unique in stg.premium_transactions.
4) If a product's lob_code is NULL, legacy would produce a NULL lob_code key. The NOT NULL lob_code column would then fail the INSERT, and the procedure would raise an error. The Spark version would output that row instead. Join keys are already upper-cased and trimmed in #pol, so the joins between the derived sets use plain equality. Joins against raw source columns (products, fx currency, brokers) use upper(rtrim()).
5) COUNT results are cast to int, matching the INT columns.
